facts: Read the domain from the left-most to the right-most $x$ the graph reaches, and the range from its lowest to highest $y$.
A closed endpoint $\bullet$ is **included**, shown by $\leq$ or $\geq$ and a square bracket.
Interval notation lists the smallest value first: $-2 \leq x \leq 2$ is $[-2, 2]$, $y > 0$ is $(0, \infty)$, and all real values is $(-\infty, \infty)$.
The lowest or highest $y$ may occur at a turning point inside the graph, not only at the ends.
steps: Find the domain: read the smallest and largest $x$-values the graph reaches (its shadow on the $x$-axis).
Find the range: read the smallest and largest $y$-values the graph reaches (its shadow on the $y$-axis).
Check each endpoint: closed (included) or open/arrow (excluded).
Write each as an inequality, then in interval notation.
